excerpt: Gusto runs payroll, benefits and HR for US small businesses. Its published plans and prices, its history from ZenPayroll to a $9.3 billion valuation, and alternatives.
content:
Gusto is payroll, benefits and HR software for small and medium-sized businesses in the United States. It pays employees and contractors, calculates, files and pays payroll taxes, and handles new-hire paperwork, time off, health insurance and other benefits. It can also pay contractors in more than 120 countries.

The company started as ZenPayroll, founded in 2011 by Josh Reeves, Edward Kim and Tomer London, and went through Y Combinator's Winter 2012 batch. The company was later renamed Gusto. Reeves is chief executive, Kim chief technology officer and London chief product officer.

Gusto is private. In June 2025 Fortune reported that it ran a tender offer of more than $200 million for current and former employees, led by Teachers' Venture Growth, part of the Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, at the company's last valuation of $9.3 billion.

Pricing is a monthly base fee plus a fee per person paid, and Gusto says it is month-to-month with no long-term contract. The three main plans differ mostly in whether you can run payroll in more than one state and how much HR support and compliance help is included. Note that Gusto's full payroll service is for US employers; it is not a payroll tool for companies employing staff in India.

We have not used Gusto for this page. It brings together Gusto's own website and pricing page and reporting from the outlets linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from.

use_cases: Running US payroll with tax filings handled
Paying contractors in the US and abroad
Onboarding new hires and storing documents
Offering health insurance and other benefits through Gusto's brokers

fit: US small businesses that want payroll, taxes and basic HR in one place
startups with US employees in one or several states
companies paying a mix of employees and contractors
not_fit: companies paying employees in India or other countries on local payroll: Gusto's payroll is for US employers
very large enterprises with complex global HR needs

pricing.intro: Gusto's published payroll plans, in US dollars, from its pricing page. Each is a monthly base fee plus a monthly fee per person; you are charged only for active employees.

plans.name: Simple
plans.detail: Payroll in one state, unlimited payrolls, tax filings and payments, basic PTO policies

plans.name: Plus
plans.detail: Multi-state payroll, time tracking and scheduling, unlimited next-day pay, contractor invoices

plans.name: Premium
plans.detail: Named account support, HR guidance, Gusto Business Compliance, unlimited same-day and instant pay

notes: Add-ons include global contractor payments ($5 per payment to US bank accounts), Priority Support ($30/month + $3 per person on Simple and Plus) and Gusto Business Compliance ($85/month per state on an annual contract, included in Premium).
A separate Gusto Solo plan covers S-corp owners paying themselves.

alternatives.intro: Other payroll and HR platforms for US businesses.

items.name: Rippling
items.what: HR, IT and finance platform with payroll
items.difference: A broader suite that combines HR and payroll with IT and finance tools.

items.name: ADP RUN
items.difference: Payroll from ADP, one of the largest US payroll providers.

items.name: QuickBooks Payroll
items.difference: Fits businesses already doing their accounts in QuickBooks.

items.name: Deel
items.difference: Built for hiring and paying people in many countries.

pros: Transparent published pricing and month-to-month billing
Tax filing and payments included on every plan
Payroll, benefits and HR in one product
cons: Per-person fees add up as a team grows
Multi-state payroll needs Plus or above
US-focused: not a local payroll tool for other countries

faq.a: Simple is $49 a month plus $6 per person, Plus $80 plus $12, and Premium $180 plus $22, according to Gusto's pricing page on 15 October 2026.
Josh Reeves, Edward Kim and Tomer London founded it in 2011 as ZenPayroll.
Gusto's payroll is for US employers. It can pay contractors in more than 120 countries, but it does not run local Indian payroll.
Fortune reported that its June 2025 employee tender offer was done at its last valuation, $9.3 billion. Gusto is private.
